text: Tuesday it felt like a calling.
Cairn sat down like the pile had chosen him.
The chair was already pulled in.
The files were already open.
He treated the first hour like proof.
This is the one.
This is the work his life was waiting for.
The spark was loud enough to drown the dull parts.
He even told a friend.
I think I found it.
He said it like a discovery, not like a plan.
The pile looked back at him with the same heat.
He stayed past the time he had blocked.
He did not notice the chair.
He did not notice the clock.
Calling will do that.
It makes the body sit as if the work were already a home.
Thursday the same pile felt like homework.
Same desk.
Same files.
Same chair.
The spark had gone quiet.
A hard paragraph sat there and did not love him back.
The sentence that used to pull him now asked him to carry it.
Cairn felt the old verdict form in his mouth.
Hard must mean I picked the wrong thing.
He almost closed the lid.
He almost told that friend it was a false alarm.
He almost went hunting for a cleaner calling on the same night.
He stood up once.
He sat down again.
The folder had not moved.
The verdict had.
He does not close the lid.
Hard does not mean you picked the wrong thing.
Finish the session anyway.
The spark dying is the job, not the warning.
Tuesday was allowed to feel like a calling.
Thursday is allowed to feel like work.
Those two days are one pile.
Cairn will name the theory that is talking.
Then he will stay long enough to finish the block he already started.
He will not ask the room for a new passion before the hour is done.
